root_cause.text: The `ceph_mdsc_build_path()` function failed to free the memory allocated by `__getname()` for the "path" buffer in multiple error return paths, causing memory leaks when the function returned error codes before transferring ownership of the pointer to the caller.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `__putname(path)` calls before three `return ERR_PTR()` statements in error paths where the allocated path buffer was not being freed. These error paths occur when: (1) an encryption operation fails, (2) a path length calculation fails, and (3) the constructed path exceeds PATH_MAX. In all cases, the path pointer allocated at the start of the function was being returned as an error without proper cleanup, violating the resource ownership contract that requires the function to free the buffer if it doesn't pass ownership to the caller via `path_info.path`.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 550f7ca98ee028a606aa75705a7e77b1bd11720f
Author: Max Kellermann <max.kellermann@ionos.com>
Date:   Mon Nov 18 23:28:28 2024 +0100

    ceph: give up on paths longer than PATH_MAX
    
    If the full path to be built by ceph_mdsc_build_path() happens to be
    longer than PATH_MAX, then this function will enter an endless (retry)
    loop, effectively blocking the whole task.  Most of the machine
    becomes unusable, making this a very simple and effective DoS
    vulnerability.
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit removes the problematic retry loop that caused an endless loop when paths exceeded PATH_MAX. The vulnerable construct was the 'goto retry;' statement at line 2808 in the original code, which would cause the function to loop indefinitely when pos < 0 (indicating the path buffer was too small). This commit replaces that retry with 'return ERR_PTR(-ENAMETOOLONG);', which properly exits the function with an error code instead of looping. The fix also addresses the memory leak issue mentioned in the root cause by ensuring the function returns early with proper error handling rather than retrying indefinitely. The code shown is sufficient to determine that this commit introduces the fix for the vulnerability rather than introducing the bug.
